import Mathlib

structure CycleGraph where
  adj : Array (Array Nat)

def CycleGraph.well_formed (g : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.adj.size →
    ∀ v, v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → v < g.adj.size

def CycleGraph.size (g : CycleGraph) : Nat :=
  g.adj.size

def CycleGraph.has_edge (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) : Prop :=
  u < g.adj.size ∧
  v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[]

def CycleGraph.is_path (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  p.length > 0 ∧
  ∀ i, i + 1 < p.length →
    g.has_edge (p.getD i 0) (p.getD (i + 1) 0)

def CycleGraph.is_cycle (g : CycleGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  g.is_path p ∧ p.length > 1 ∧ p.head? = p.getLast?

def CycleGraph.graph_has_cycle (g : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, g.is_cycle p

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def has_cycle_precond (graph : CycleGraph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  graph.well_formed
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
namespace CycleGraph

/-- Boolean edge test. -/
def E (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[])

/-- One relaxation step: keep the vertices having an out-neighbour in `S`. -/
def step (g : CycleGraph) (S : List Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range g.adj.size).filter (fun v => S.any (fun w => g.E v w))

/-- `iter g k` is the list of vertices from which a walk of length `k` starts. -/
def iter (g : CycleGraph) : Nat → List Nat
  | 0 => List.range g.adj.size
  | k + 1 => g.step (g.iter k)

/-- `f` describes a walk of length `k` (`f 0 → f 1 → ... → f k`). -/
def Wk (g : CycleGraph) (f : Nat → Nat) (k : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, i < k → g.E (f i) (f (i + 1)) = true

end CycleGraph
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def has_cycle (graph : CycleGraph)
    (h_precond : has_cycle_precond graph) : Bool :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  !(graph.iter graph.adj.size).isEmpty
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def has_cycle_postcond (graph : CycleGraph) (result : Bool)
    (_ : has_cycle_precond graph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result = graph.graph_has_cycle
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
namespace CycleGraph

lemma E_iff_mem (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) :
    g.E u v = true ↔ v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] := by
  simp [E]

lemma lt_of_E (g : CycleGraph) {u v : Nat} (h : g.E u v = true) : u < g.adj.size := by
  by_contra hc
  rw [E_iff_mem] at h
  simp [Array.getD, hc] at h

lemma has_edge_iff (g : CycleGraph) (u v : Nat) :
    g.has_edge u v ↔ g.E u v = true := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (E_iff_mem g u v).mpr h.2
  · intro h
    exact ⟨lt_of_E g h, (E_iff_mem g u v).mp h⟩

lemma lt_of_E_target (g : CycleGraph) (hwf : g.well_formed) {u v : Nat}
    (h : g.E u v = true) : v < g.adj.size :=
  hwf u (lt_of_E g h) v ((E_iff_mem g u v).mp h)

lemma getD_map_range (f : Nat → Nat) (L t : Nat) (h : t < L) :
    ((List.range L).map f).getD t 0 = f t := by
  rw [List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (by simpa using h)]
  simp

lemma ne_nil_iff_exists_mem (l : List Nat) : l ≠ [] ↔ ∃ v, v ∈ l := by
  cases l with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t => exact ⟨fun _ => ⟨a, by simp⟩, fun _ => by simp⟩

lemma mem_iter_of (g : CycleGraph) (hwf : g.well_formed) :
    ∀ k (f : Nat → Nat), f 0 < g.adj.size → g.Wk f k → f 0 ∈ g.iter k := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
      intro f h _
      simpa [iter] using h
  | succ k ih =>
      intro f h hw
      have he : g.E (f 0) (f 1) = true := hw 0 (by omega)
      have h1 : f 1 < g.adj.size := lt_of_E_target g hwf he
      have hw' : g.Wk (fun m => f (m + 1)) k := by
        intro i hi
        exact hw (i + 1) (by omega)
      have hm : f 1 ∈ g.iter k := by
        have := ih (fun m => f (m + 1)) (by simpa using h1) hw'
        simpa using this
      simp only [iter, step, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, List.any_eq_true]
      exact ⟨h, f 1, hm, he⟩

lemma of_mem_iter (g : CycleGraph) :
    ∀ k v, v ∈ g.iter k → v < g.adj.size ∧ ∃ f, f 0 = v ∧ g.Wk f k := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
      intro v hv
      simp only [iter, List.mem_range] at hv
      exact ⟨hv, fun _ => v, rfl, by intro i hi; omega⟩
  | succ k ih =>
      intro v hv
      simp only [iter, step, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, List.any_eq_true] at hv
      obtain ⟨hlt, w, hw2, hw1⟩ := hv
      obtain ⟨-, f, hf0, hfw⟩ := ih w hw2
      refine ⟨hlt, fun m => if m = 0 then v else f (m - 1), by simp, ?_⟩
      intro i hi
      cases i with
      | zero =>
          simpa [hf0] using hw1
      | succ j =>
          simpa using hfw j (by omega)

lemma Wk_lt (g : CycleGraph) (hwf : g.well_formed) {f : Nat → Nat} {k : Nat}
    (hw : g.Wk f k) (h0 : f 0 < g.adj.size) : ∀ i, i ≤ k → f i < g.adj.size := by
  intro i
  cases i with
  | zero => intro _; exact h0
  | succ j => intro hj; exact lt_of_E_target g hwf (hw j (by omega))

lemma cycle_of_Wk (g : CycleGraph) {f : Nat → Nat}
    (hw : g.Wk f g.adj.size) (hlt : ∀ i, i ≤ g.adj.size → f i < g.adj.size) :
    g.graph_has_cycle := by
  set n := g.adj.size with hn
  have key : ∀ a b : Nat, a < b → b ≤ n → f a = f b → g.graph_has_cycle := by
    intro a b hab hbn hfe
    refine ⟨(List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun m => f (a + m)), ⟨by simp, ?_⟩, by simp; omega, ?_⟩
    · intro i hi
      simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range] at hi
      rw [getD_map_range _ _ _ (by omega), getD_map_range _ _ _ (by omega),
        has_edge_iff]
      have : a + i < n := by omega
      have h2 := hw (a + i) this
      have h3 : a + (i + 1) = a + i + 1 := by omega
      rw [h3]
      exact h2
    · rw [List.head?_eq_getElem?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?]
      have hL : ((List.range (b - a + 1)).map (fun m => f (a + m))).length = b - a + 1 := by
        simp
      rw [hL]
      simp only [List.getElem?_map, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
      have e1 : (List.range (b - a + 1))[0]? = some 0 := by
        rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by simp)]
        simp
      have e2 : (List.range (b - a + 1))[b - a]? = some (b - a) := by
        rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by simp)]
        simp
      rw [e1, e2]
      have hb2 : a + (b - a) = b := by omega
      simp [hb2, hfe]
  obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab, hfab⟩ :=
    Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to (s := Finset.range (n + 1))
      (t := Finset.range n) (by simp) (f := f)
      (fun x hx => Finset.mem_range.mpr
        (hlt x (by have := Finset.mem_range.mp hx; omega)))
  simp only [Finset.mem_range] at ha hb
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge a b with h | h
  · exact key a b h (by omega) hfab
  · exact key b a (by omega) (by omega) hfab.symm

lemma Wk_of_cycle (g : CycleGraph) {p : List Nat} (hc : g.is_cycle p) :
    ∃ f : Nat → Nat, f 0 < g.adj.size ∧ ∀ k, g.Wk f k := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hpos, hedge⟩, hlen, hhl⟩ := hc
  have hL1 : 1 ≤ p.length - 1 := by omega
  set L := p.length - 1 with hL
  have hlast : p.getD L 0 = p.getD 0 0 := by
    rw [List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (by omega), List.getD_eq_getElem _ _ (by omega)]
    rw [List.head?_eq_getElem?, List.getLast?_eq_getElem?] at hhl
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega), List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)] at hhl
    simpa using hhl.symm
  refine ⟨fun m => p.getD (m % L) 0, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have h := (hedge 0 (by omega)).1
    simpa using h
  · intro k i _
    rw [← has_edge_iff]
    show g.has_edge (p.getD (i % L) 0) (p.getD ((i + 1) % L) 0)
    have hdm : L * (i / L) + i % L = i := Nat.div_add_mod i L
    have hmod : i % L < L := Nat.mod_lt i (by omega)
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge (i % L + 1) L with h | h
    · have hi : i + 1 = L * (i / L) + (i % L + 1) := by omega
      have : (i + 1) % L = i % L + 1 := by
        rw [hi, Nat.mul_add_mod, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h]
      rw [this]
      exact hedge (i % L) (by omega)
    · have hEq : i % L + 1 = L := by omega
      have hi : i + 1 = L * (i / L) + L := by omega
      have h0 : (i + 1) % L = 0 := by
        rw [hi, Nat.add_mod_right, Nat.mul_mod_right]
      rw [h0]
      have hed := hedge (i % L) (by omega)
      rw [hEq] at hed
      rwa [hlast] at hed

end CycleGraph
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem has_cycle_postcond_satisfied (graph : CycleGraph)
    (h_precond : has_cycle_precond graph) :
    has_cycle_postcond graph (has_cycle graph h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have key : (has_cycle graph h_precond = true) ↔ graph.graph_has_cycle := by
    constructor
    · intro h
      simp only [has_cycle, Bool.not_eq_true', List.isEmpty_eq_false_iff] at h
      obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := (CycleGraph.ne_nil_iff_exists_mem _).mp h
      obtain ⟨hvlt, f, hf0, hfw⟩ := CycleGraph.of_mem_iter graph _ v hv
      refine CycleGraph.cycle_of_Wk graph hfw ?_
      exact CycleGraph.Wk_lt graph h_precond hfw (by rw [hf0]; exact hvlt)
    · intro hcy
      obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hcy
      obtain ⟨f, hf0, hfw⟩ := CycleGraph.Wk_of_cycle graph hp
      have hm := CycleGraph.mem_iter_of graph h_precond graph.adj.size f hf0 (hfw _)
      simp only [has_cycle, Bool.not_eq_true', List.isEmpty_eq_false_iff]
      exact (CycleGraph.ne_nil_iff_exists_mem _).mpr ⟨f 0, hm⟩
  rw [has_cycle_postcond, eq_iff_iff]
  exact key
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What I implemented

The algorithm is a length-indexed reachability DP (no `sorry`, no oracle, no `decide` over the target property):

- `E g u v` — boolean edge test on the adjacency array.
- `iter g k` — the list of vertices from which a walk of exactly `k` edges starts:
  - `iter 0 = List.range n` (every vertex),
  - `iter (k+1) = {v < n | ∃ w ∈ iter k, E v w}`.
- `has_cycle graph = !(graph.iter graph.adj.size).isEmpty`

i.e. the graph has a cycle iff some vertex admits a walk of `n` edges. Termination is structural in `k`, so no cycle-guard is needed.

## Proof structure (in the `lemma` section)

- `has_edge_iff`, `lt_of_E`, `lt_of_E_target` — bridge the spec's `has_edge` with the boolean `E`, using well-formedness for target bounds.
- `mem_iter_of` / `of_mem_iter` — `v ∈ iter k ↔ v < n ∧ ∃ f, f 0 = v ∧ Wk f k`, where `Wk f k` says `f 0 → … → f k` is a walk. Both by induction on `k`.
- `Wk_lt` — all walk vertices stay `< n`.
- `cycle_of_Wk` (**soundness**): from a walk of `n` edges among `n` vertices, `Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to` gives indices `a < b` with `f a = f b`; the segment `(List.range (b-a+1)).map (f ∘ (a + ·))` is exhibited as a cycle satisfying `is_path`, `length > 1`, and `head? = getLast?`.
- `Wk_of_cycle` (**completeness**): from a cycle `p` of `L = p.length - 1` edges, the periodic map `m ↦ p.getD (m % L) 0` is a walk of *every* length — the wrap-around step uses `head? = getLast?` — so that vertex lands in `iter n`.

The final theorem converts the `Bool`/`Prop` postcondition with `eq_iff_iff` and discharges both directions from these lemmas. Only the four marker sections were edited; all markers are preserved.

Semantically, this is a valid graph-theoretic algorithm:
- `iter k` characterizes vertices from which there exists a walk of length `k`.
- If there is a vertex from which a walk of length `n = |V|` starts, then by pigeonhole principle some vertex repeats along that walk, yielding a directed cycle.
- Conversely, if there is a directed cycle, then one can loop around it to obtain walks of arbitrary length, in particular length `n`, so `iter n` is nonempty.
